# AlphaGo {.smaller}

> **The image.** A chess player who plays themselves a million times overnight,
> and wakes up smarter than they were.

[2016: beat the world's best Go player a decade before anyone expected.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** Monte Carlo Tree Search + a policy network (which moves to consider) + a value network (who's winning) + self-play (the engine is its own training partner).]{.body}

[The pattern of *search guided by a learned heuristic* keeps showing up. Modern LLM "thinking" modes are quietly running cousins of this loop.]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## AlphaGo: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ AlphaGo (top)]{.up-cue}

- Lead with the chess image. Let it land.
- Pause on **"wakes up smarter than they were."** Does most of the work.
- Walk the recipe in order: MCTS → policy → value → self-play.
- Each technical term gets one plain-English line. *Imagine playing the position a thousand times in your head, randomly...*
- Don't apologize for skipping math.
- Mention **AlphaZero** generalized this (chess, shogi); **MuZero** learned the rules from scratch.
- Land the pattern: **search + learned heuristic** is in modern LLM "thinking" modes.
- Tee up: first of four totally different stacks coming.

# AlphaFold {.smaller}

> **The image.** Origami, but the paper is a sentence of amino acids and the
> final shape decides whether the protein heals you or kills you.

[2020: cracked a 50-year-old grand challenge in biology. 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** a transformer that reasons about which amino-acid positions are talking to each other, plus a *geometry-aware* network that respects rotations and translations. Output: atom coordinates accurate enough for drug discovery.]{.body}

[The architecture is **transformers + GNN + geometric deep learning** stacked. Not just one trick.]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## AlphaFold: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ AlphaFold (top)]{.up-cue}

- Ground audience first: proteins fold; **shape IS function**. Everything in your body is proteins.
- Origami metaphor: paper is amino acids, fold determines what it does.
- Walk recipe: input (sequence + related-protein search) → **Evoformer** (talks-to-which) → **Structure module** (atom coordinates).
- Stress the geometric / **equivariant** piece. *Turn the molecule, prediction turns the same way.* That's the load-bearing trick.
- **2024 Nobel in Chemistry** lands here.
- Architecture point: transformers + GNN + geometry, all stacked. Not one trick.
- Real-world: drug discovery, enzyme engineering, materials. Free database online.

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

# Stable Diffusion {.smaller}

> **The image.** Start with TV static. Squint at it until you see a cat. Squint
> harder, and the cat sharpens. The model is the trained squint.

[2022: image generation went from "research toy" to a phone app.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** train a network to undo *one step* of noise. To generate, start from pure static and run the network many times, conditioned on a text prompt at each step.]{.body}

[Generation is **denoising**, not prediction. A different paradigm wearing a familiar product.]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Stable Diffusion: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Stable Diffusion (top)]{.up-cue}

- Lean into the **TV static → squint** metaphor.
- This is the moment the audience leans in. They've all used it; nobody told them what's under the hood.
- Walk recipe: forward (add noise step by step) → reverse (network undoes one step at a time) → generation is many small denoising steps.
- Latent diffusion is the trick that put it on a consumer GPU.
- Stress: generation is **denoising, not prediction**. Different math, different paradigm.
- Name the math: **score-based / SDEs / Langevin**.
- Generalized fast: video (Sora, Veo), audio, 3D, **proteins (RFdiffusion)**.
- Tee up: this is an **energy-based model** in disguise. Next section picks that up.

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

# AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry {.smaller}

> **The image.** Pair-programming with a mathematician: one half guesses, the
> other half proves. Guess fast, check slow.

[2024: silver-medal level on the International Math Olympiad.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** a neural network proposes candidate proof steps; a formal verifier (Lean, or a custom geometry engine) accepts or rejects each one. The neural side learns from the verdicts.]{.body}

[Pattern-matching **plus** provable correctness. Neither alone is enough.]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ AlphaProof / AlphaGeometry (top)]{.up-cue}

- Pair-programming image. Most of the room has done it.
- **Guess fast, check slow** is the punchline. Say it explicitly.
- Walk the loop: neural proposes (creative, often wrong) → formal verifier accepts/rejects → neural learns from verdicts.
- Geometry uses a custom symbolic engine; algebra/number-theory uses **Lean**.
- **IMO silver-medal** matters because you cannot bluff. Answers must be provable.
- Stress: pattern-matching alone hits a ceiling; pure logic alone hits a ceiling; the space between is interesting.
- Tee up: this is the concrete **neurosymbolic** story. Section 2 picks it up.

# Stacks, not tricks {.smaller}

Every system we just walked through is **multiple paradigms stacked**:

- AlphaGo = MCTS + deep RL + self-play
- AlphaFold = transformers + GNN + geometric deep learning
- Stable Diffusion = score-based / diffusion + U-Net + text conditioning
- AlphaProof = neural search + symbolic verifier

[So: let's look at the paradigms themselves.]{.accent-magenta}

# Evolutionary methods {.smaller}

> **The image.** Throw a thousand random solutions at the wall. Keep the ones
> that stick. Mash them together. Repeat for a few thousand generations.
> Survival pressure does the rest.

[No gradients. No backprop. Just selection.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** maintain a population of candidates, score each by a fitness function, then apply selection, mutation, and recombination to produce the next generation. Variants: **GA** (bits), **ES / CMA-ES** (continuous), **NEAT** (evolves network topology), **GP** (evolves programs), **swarm** (collective behavior).]{.body}

[Embarrassingly parallel. Works on black-box, discrete, non-differentiable problems where SGD can't go.]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Evolutionary methods: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Evolutionary methods (top)]{.up-cue}

- Walk the **thousand-on-the-wall** metaphor. Survival pressure does the rest.
- "**No gradients**" is the punchline. Say it.
- Recipe: population → fitness → **selection / mutation / recombination**.
- Name the variants briefly: GA (bits), ES / CMA-ES (continuous), NEAT (evolves topology), GP (evolves programs), swarm (collective).
- **Embarrassingly parallel** is the big practical win.
- Use cases: architecture search, robotics controllers (sparse reward), antenna/circuit/scheduling design.
- The eyebrow-raiser: **OpenAI 2017** showed ES competitive with deep RL on Atari.
- Tee up: this is the **substrate** for the deep dive at 3:50.

# Energy-based models {.smaller}

> **The image.** A landscape of hills and valleys. Drop a marble anywhere. It
> rolls downhill. The valleys are the things the model thinks are *real*.

[Train the landscape; let physics handle generation.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** define an energy function over configurations. Training lowers the energy of real data and raises it for everything else. Generation rolls downhill from a random start. **Diffusion models** are a special case: they learn the local slope of the landscape (the *score*).]{.body}

[Hopfield networks (associative memory) won the **2024 Nobel Prize in Physics**.]{.accent-amber}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Energy-based models: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Energy-based models (top)]{.up-cue}

- Marble-rolling-into-valley image. Let it land.
- Stress: **train the landscape**, let physics handle generation.
- Recipe: define energy function → train so real data sits in valleys → generate by rolling downhill.
- Diffusion is a **special case**: it learns the local slope (the score). Callback to Stable Diffusion.
- **2024 Physics Nobel** (Hopfield) lands here. Don't undersell this; it's the moment the room realizes EBMs were under the hood the whole time.
- The math is **physics, not linguistics**. Different intuitions, different limits.
- Where it shows up: image / video / audio / 3D / protein backbones, associative memory, anomaly detection.
- New theory of "what does a model know": not "predict next token" but "sit at low energy near plausible data."

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

# Neurosymbolic AI {.smaller}

> **The image.** A musician who can also read sheet music. The ear catches
> what's there; the page catches what *has* to be there.

[Perception **plus** logic. Intuition **plus** proof.]{.muted}

[**Recipe:** combine neural front-ends (good at perception, fuzzy pattern-matching) with symbolic back-ends (good at logic, composition, provable correctness). Architectures vary: neural-then-symbolic pipelines, differentiable logic, program synthesis with neural priors, **LLM + formal verifier** (AlphaProof).]{.body}

[**Bet:** pure pattern-matching hits a ceiling, pure logic hits a ceiling, and the interesting space is between them.]{.accent-magenta}

# Research Deep Dive {.section-title background-color="#12132A"}

[3:50 to 4:30 · hierarchical evolutionary systems with orchestration]{.muted}

# Why hierarchy, why evolution, why orchestration {.smaller}

- **Why evolution.** Gradients require a smooth, differentiable objective. Most interesting objectives aren't.
- **Why hierarchy.** Search at a single scale plateaus. Stack search inside search, and the plateau breaks.
- **Why orchestration at the top.** The upper layer's job isn't to *solve*. It's to *decide which layer below is solving the right problem*.

[Thesis: **stacked search, glued together by something that can reason about the stack itself.**]{.accent-magenta}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Why this shape: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Why hierarchy / evolution / orchestration (top)]{.up-cue}

- **Don't rush this slide.** The motivation sells the rest of the section.
- Walk each "why" deliberately.
- *Why evolution:* gradients need smoothness. Real things rarely are. Composability, novelty, sparse reward, long-horizon credit. Gradient descent struggles in all of them.
- *Why hierarchy:* single-scale search plateaus. A second loop *above* the first can evolve the first's configurations. Now the system climbs both fitness AND fitness-definition.
- *Why orchestration:* pure stacked search has no notion of "what are we trying to do right now." Orchestrator reads the stack and re-aims.
- Thesis line: **stacked search + something that reasons about the stack.**
- If the room is with you on *why*, the architecture diagram does the rest.

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Why this shape: further reading {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Why hierarchy / evolution / orchestration (top)]{.up-cue}

- Lehman & Stanley, *Abandoning Objectives: Evolution Through the Search for Novelty Alone.* [paper](https://www.cs.swarthmore.edu/~meeden/DevelopmentalRobotics/lehman_ecj11.pdf)
- Wang et al., *POET: Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer.* [arXiv:1901.01753](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.01753)

# Architecture sketch {.smaller}

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  subgraph L0["L0 · Substrate"]
    P0["Population of solutions"]
    F0["Fitness eval"]
    P0 --> F0 --> P0
  end
  subgraph L1["L1 · Strategy"]
    P1["Population of L0 configurations"]
    F1["Meta-fitness"]
    P1 --> F1 --> P1
  end
  subgraph L2["L2 · Goal"]
    P2["Population of L1 objectives"]
    F2["Outer signal"]
    P2 --> F2 --> P2
  end
  ORCH(("Orchestrator")):::accent
  ORCH -. directs .-> L2
  ORCH -. directs .-> L1
  ORCH -. directs .-> L0
  L0 --> L1 --> L2 --> ORCH

  classDef accent fill:#9B5CFF,stroke:#FF4FCB,color:#08080F;
```

[Three rungs · an orchestrator that reads the stack and adjusts pressure.]{.muted}

[speaker notes below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Architecture sketch: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Architecture sketch (top)]{.up-cue}

- **Walk the diagram bottom-up.**
- **L0 (Substrate):** population + fitness loop. Real evolutionary engine. Whatever your "do the task" layer is.
- **L1 (Strategy):** evolves L0's *configurations*. What population size, mutation rate, fitness function? L1 candidates ARE those configurations.
- **L2 (Goal):** evolves L1's *objectives*. What is L1 even optimizing for? L2 candidates are answers to that.
- **Orchestrator:** sits above all three. Reads behavior, directs pressure. In our prototype: an **LLM with tools**. Cheap to iterate on.
- Stress: the orchestrator is what makes this an **AI system** and not just nested optimization.
- Compare to **predictive processing hierarchy**: low-level predictions feed up, high-level corrections feed down. Same shape.

# What's working, what's open {.smaller}

**Working**

- The substrate-level loop runs and converges on toy problems.
- The orchestrator-as-LLM-with-tools framing has been useful for prototyping the upper layer cheaply.
- Mapping the architecture onto consciousness research (self-models, predictive processing) is producing testable questions.

**Open**

- **Credit assignment across layers.** When the outer signal fires, which rung deserves the update?
- **Compute.** Naively, hierarchy multiplies population by generations. Need shortcuts.
- **Evaluation.** What does "working" mean for a system whose objective is generated by another part of itself?
- **Orchestrator stability.** The upper layer is the only non-evolutionary piece. Should it be?

[Honest: this is a research program, not a product. Yet.]{.muted}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## What's working / open: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ What's working, what's open (top)]{.up-cue}

- Lead **honest**. This is research, not a product. Don't oversell.
- On *credit assignment*: outer signal fires, but L0/L1/L2 each need to know their contribution. Candidates: hindsight relabeling, lineage tracking, novelty credit, Pareto fronts.
- On *compute*: inner loop runs hundreds of generations per outer eval; compute multiplies fast. Tactics: shared substrate populations, surrogate fitness, importance sampling, multi-fidelity.
- On *evaluation*: standard ML assumes fixed test set. This system *generates* its own criteria. Open-ended evolution lit (POET, QD) is the closest established work.
- On *orchestrator stability*: it's currently the only non-evolutionary piece. Genuine open question whether it should be evolved too, or whether some non-evolutionary structure is load-bearing.
- Anchor: this is where the **deep dive discussion** lives. Don't try to resolve, hand it to the room.

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

# Touchpoints with consciousness research {.smaller}

- **Predictive processing.** Agents that minimize a single quantity (free energy) look a lot like a hierarchy with an orchestrator.
- **Active inference.** The Friston program. Mathematically demanding, philosophically ambitious, increasingly relevant.
- **Open-ended evolution.** Does the system keep generating *novel* fitness regimes, or does it converge?
- The honest version: we don't know what consciousness is, but we have hypotheses with empirical handles now.

[I work on this part-time at Ardea. Augs is the planned product wrapper.]{.accent-cyan}

[speaker notes & further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Consciousness research: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Consciousness research (top)]{.up-cue}

- *Predictive processing:* brain (or any rich agent) constantly predicts inputs, updates the model on prediction errors. Perception, action, learning, attention - same operation under the hood: **minimize surprise**.
- Hierarchical shape: low-level predictions feed up, high-level corrections feed down. **Same shape as the architecture sketch.**
- *Active inference (Friston):* agent acts to make inputs match predictions. Under the right priors, this looks like curiosity, planning, homeostasis. Single math, multiple behaviors.
- Why it matters here: gives a single optimization principle that can ground subjective experience.
- *Open-ended evolution:* most systems converge. Consciousness doesn't. Keeps generating new problems for itself. POET / QD are the closest models.
- **Honest framing:** we don't know what consciousness IS. We have hypotheses with empirical hooks now.
- Land Ardea / Augs as the product wrapper for this research.

[further reading below ↓]{.detail-hint}

# Discussion prompts {.smaller}

1. Should the orchestrator itself be evolved, or is some non-evolutionary structure load-bearing?
2. Is hierarchy enough, or do we need **lateral** structure too (peer layers, not just stacked)?
3. Where does **active inference** belong in this picture: a fourth layer, or the *binding agent* across layers?
4. The honest one: how do we tell if this is **actually intelligent** vs. cleverly-engineered hill-climbing?

[speaker notes below ↓]{.detail-hint}

## Discussion prompts: speaker notes {.smaller .detail-slide}

[↑ Discussion prompts (top)]{.up-cue}

- Read them all up front, then pick whichever the room reacts to most.
- **Prompt 4 is the one that usually surfaces the most interesting pushback.** Hold it for last if the room is quiet on the others.
- Don't try to resolve anything. Let people argue.
- If the discussion drifts into "is this AGI" territory, fine, but bring it back to the architecture.
- Capture interesting threads for mingling later.
- Time-box: 20 minutes max here before the wrap, otherwise Q&A gets crushed.
